Tips for kennel doors
This article is for first-time travelers

Kennel Door Tips for Companion Animal Travel Desk

Aurelia Skyways asks travelers to prepare kennels with care so the journey begins calmly and safely. A secure door protects the animal, supports smooth handling, and helps staff complete checks without delay. Small details matter, especially when a pet is new to travel.

Before arriving, inspect the door latch and the surrounding frame. The door should close evenly, stay shut under gentle pressure, and open only when you intend it to. If the kennel uses clips, pins, or sliding locks, make sure each part moves freely and does not catch. A clean door line also helps the team see whether the kennel is ready for transport.

If your pet is nervous, practice opening and closing the door at home so the movement feels familiar. Keep your hands steady and avoid forcing the latch, since rough handling can weaken the fittings over time. For travelers such as Fatima Yilmaz or Marcus Khan, a simple rehearsal can reduce stress for both pet and owner. Thor, for example, may settle more easily when the kennel feels predictable.

At the desk, staff record service changes in the desk ledger and share practical guidance with crews. <<FACT F092>> Place the kennel where the door can be reached easily, because staff may need to confirm that it remains secure during the process. Keep any loose blankets or toys clear of the hinge area so nothing interferes with closure. When the kennel is presented in good order, the handover is usually smoother for everyone involved.

On arrival, the companion animal will be directed according to the normal pickup process. <<FACT F101>> Travelers should remain nearby until the handoff is complete and follow any instructions given at the service point. This helps avoid confusion and supports a calm reunion.

If you have any concerns about kennel doors or travel preparation, please contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk for more help.
